Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verse 10–17:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And when your Lord called out to Musa﴾: that is, remember, O our Messenger, for your people, when your Lord called out to Musa.

﴿Go﴾: that is, go to the wrongdoing people.

﴿Will they not fear Allah?﴾: will they not be wary of God, their Lord and the Lord of their forefathers of old? What is wrong with them, what has befallen them?

﴿My chest will be constricted﴾: that is, because of their denial of me.

﴿And my tongue will not speak freely﴾: that is, because of the impediment that is in it.

﴿So send for Harun﴾: that is, for my brother Harun, so that he may be with me in conveying my message.

﴿And they have a charge against me﴾: that is, the charge of the Copt whom Musa killed before his departure to Madyan.

﴿He said: "No!"﴾: that is, God Most High said to him, "No," meaning they will not kill you.

﴿So go, you both﴾: you and Harun.

﴿We are messengers of the Lord of the worlds﴾: that is, sent to you.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High, ﴿And when your Lord called out to Musa﴾: this is the beginning of a series of narratives, beginning with the story of Musa and concluding with the story of Shu'ayb, which he related to the polytheists so that they might witness its events and understand its outcomes, namely the destruction and annihilation of those who deny, however great their strength and however long their lives. The Most High said, addressing His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿And when your Lord called out to Musa﴾: that is, remember when your Lord called out to Musa on a cold winter night, in the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree. ﴿That you go to the wrongdoing people, the people of Pharaoh﴾: for they wronged themselves by disbelief and polytheism, and wronged the Children of Israel by persecuting and torturing them. ﴿Will they not fear Allah?﴾: that is, say to them, "Will you not fear Allah?", that is, command them to be mindful of their Lord by believing in Him, affirming His oneness, and ceasing to wrong His servants; the interrogative here carries the sense of a command. And the Most High said, ﴿He said: "My Lord, I fear that they will deny me"﴾: that is, Musa said after being commissioned, "My Lord, I fear that they will deny what I tell them and call them to." ﴿And my chest will be constricted﴾ because of that, ﴿and my tongue will not speak freely﴾ because of the impediment in it. Accordingly, ﴿so send for Harun﴾: that is, Jibril should convey to him that he should be with me as a helper in conveying my message. As for His words, ﴿And they have a charge against me, so I fear that they will kill me﴾: this is the statement of Musa, peace be upon him, to his Lord, complaining to Him of his fear that they would kill him for the soul he had killed when he was in Egypt, before his departure to Madyan. The Lord, Most High, answered him, ﴿No!﴾: that is, they will not kill you. He commanded them both to proceed to Pharaoh, saying, ﴿So go, you both, with Our signs﴾: namely the staff and the hand. ﴿Indeed, We are with you, listening﴾: that is, deliver to him what I have commanded you to deliver, for I am with you, hearing what you say and what is said to you. ﴿So come to Pharaoh and say﴾ upon your arrival to him: ﴿"Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds"﴾: that is, we bring a message from Him, the content of which is that you send the Children of Israel with us, that we may take them out to the land of Sham which God promised to the Children of Israel. This is what Musa and Harun, the two messengers of the Lord of the worlds, said; as for Pharaoh's reply, it is in the verses that follow.

Guidance of the verses:

**Meaning of the Verses:**

The noble context continues with the dialogue between Musa (peace be upon him) and Fir'awn (upon whom be the curses of the Most Merciful). When Musa said, ﴿Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 46] at the beginning of the dialogue, Fir'awn asked in defiance and arrogance, ﴿And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾. That is, what thing is He, or of what kind among the kinds of created beings? Musa answered him with what Allah Most High had told of Him: ﴿The Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾, meaning the Creator of the heavens and the earth and the Creator of what is between them, and the Owner of all of that, ﴿if you are certain﴾ that every created thing must have a creator who brought it into being, a matter that sound minds do not deny. Here Fir'awn said, with contempt and pride, to those around him from among the men of his state and the nobles of his people: ﴿Do you not listen?﴾, as if what Musa said were a strange or objectionable matter. Musa perceived this and said, ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers﴾, meaning your Creator and the Creator of your earliest forefathers, all of whom are subject to His lordship, submitting to His rule and His direction.

Fir'awn was enraged and said, ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is surely mad﴾. He wanted to belittle Musa, because Musa had angered him with the words ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers﴾. So Musa replied again, saying, ﴿The Lord of the east and the west and what is between them﴾, meaning the Lord of the whole universe, ﴿if you would use your reason﴾, meaning, if you understood what is being addressed to you and said to you. In this answer was something that would tear apart Fir'awn's heart, so he responded with what Allah Most High reported of him in His words: ﴿He said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned"﴾, meaning, a lord besides me. ﴿I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾: that is, I will imprison you and place you in the depths beneath the earth with the prisoners. Musa (peace be upon him) then said, ﴿Even if I brought you something clear?﴾, meaning, will you imprison me even if I bring you a clear proof and a shining argument for the truth of what I have said and to which I call you? Here Fir'awn said what Allah Most High reported: ﴿He said, "Then bring it, if you are among the truthful"﴾, meaning in what you claim and say.

**Lessons (Hidayat) of the Verses:**

1. The establishment of Lordship (*Rububiyya*), which necessarily implies Divinity (*Uluhiyya*), through this dialogue, so that the polytheists may hear it, and know that they are preceded in polytheism and disbelief, and that they are astray.

2. It is the way of the people of falsehood to be treacherous in dispute and in speech, based on the hadith: "And when he disputes, he is treacherous."

3. The people of pride and haughtiness on earth, when arguments fail them, resort to threats, intimidation, and the use of force.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*A manifest serpent (thu'ban mubin):* a clearly visible serpent, with no doubt that it is a serpent.

*And he drew out his hand (wa nazaa yadahu):* he brought it out of his pocket after having put it in.

*A knowledgeable sorcerer (li-sahirin 'alim):* one who excels in the knowledge of magic.

*Put off (arjih) him and his brother:* postpone their matter.

*Gatherers (hashirin):* those who assemble the sorcerers.

*Every knowledgeable sorcerer (sahhar 'alim):* one who excels in the craft more than Moses.

*A appointed day (yawm ma'lum):* it is the forenoon of their festival day.

*Will you gather? (hal antum mujtami'un):* that is, gather, so that we may follow the sorcerers in their religion if they are the victors.

*And indeed you will surely be among those brought near (wa innakum idhan lamina al-muqarrabin):* that is, you will have the wage, the reward that was promised to them, and they will additionally be granted the distinction of nearness to him.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

The noble context continues with the dialogue between Moses, peace be upon him, and Pharaoh, upon whom be the curses of the Most Merciful. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verse 43–49:

Explanation of the words:

*Alqū mā antum mulqūn* (Throw down what you are throwing): He commanded them to throw, seeking to make the truth manifest.

*Mā yafikūn* (What they fabricate): i.e., what they reverse through their deception, namely that their ropes and staffs are serpents running about.

*Rabb Mūsā wa-Hārūn* (The Lord of Moses and Aaron): i.e., because they knew that what they had witnessed of the staff does not come about by means of magic.

*Min khilāf* (On alternate sides): i.e., the right hand of each and the left leg.

*Wa-la-uṣallibannakum ajma'īn* (And I will surely crucify you all): i.e., I will hang you upon wooden posts after cutting off your hands and feet on alternate sides.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues in the dialogue that took place between Moses, peace be upon him, and Pharaoh, upon whom be the curses of the All-Merciful. After the sorcerers asked Pharaoh whether they would receive a reward for contending with Moses if they prevailed, and after Pharaoh reassured them regarding the wage and the reward, Moses said to them, ﴿Throw down what you are going to throw down﴾, from the ropes and staffs in the arena. ﴿So they threw down their ropes and their staffs﴾, and they swore by the might of Pharaoh that they would surely be the victors. Indeed, the whole arena turned into serpents and vipers, until Moses sensed fear within himself. Then his Lord, exalted is He, revealed to him: throw down your staff. So he threw it, and behold, it swallowed up what they were fabricating. This is the meaning of His statement, exalted is He, in this context: ﴿So they threw down their ropes and their staffs and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed we are the victors." Then Moses threw down his staff, and suddenly it swallowed up what they were fabricating﴾. The meaning of "swallowed up what they were fabricating" is that it engulfed within itself, through its mouth, everything the sorcerers had falsely fabricated and invented by their magic, namely the transformation of the ropes and staffs into serpents and vipers. His statement, exalted is He, ﴿So the sorcerers were thrown down prostrating﴾, means that, overwhelmed by amazement and by the truth that had dazzled them, they cast themselves down upon the ground prostrating to God, exalted is He, believing in Him. They were then asked about their condition, and they said: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron﴾. Here Pharaoh feared that control would slip from his hands and that people would believe in Moses and Aaron and disbelieve in him. So he said to the sorcerers: ﴿Have you believed in Him before I give you permission?﴾, meaning: how can you believe without my permission? As though he owned that right over them, and this was merely an obvious maneuver. Then he said to them, ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾, i.e., since he was your teacher, you colluded with him to prevail, so you showed that he had defeated you, as deception and misleading of the masses. Then he threatened them, saying, ﴿But you will soon know﴾ my punishment for you for this collusion, which is ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides﴾, i.e., I will cut off from each one of you his right hand and left foot, ﴿and I will surely crucify you all﴾, so that I will leave none of you except that I hang him upon a post until he dies crucified. Did Pharaoh carry out what he threatened? God knows best.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Moses did not hasten to throw his staff first, because this was a matter of knowledge, not a matter of war. In war, seizing the initiative to take control of the battle is beneficial, but in matters of knowledge it is fitting to let the opponent go first; when he displays what he has, one attacks him with proofs and evidences, refutes him, and the truth becomes manifest and triumphs over falsehood. This is the method Moses followed, by inspiration from his Lord, exalted is He.

2- An aspect of divine guidance is the guidance of the sorcerers, for at the beginning of the day they were disbelieving sorcerers, and at its end they were righteous believers.

3- Everything Pharaoh pursued with the sorcerers was entirely of the nature of failed political maneuvers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 50–60:

Explanation of the words:

"No harm" (لا ضير): that is, there is no harm upon us.

"Returning" (لمنقلبون): that is, returning after death, and that is a joy, not a harm.

"If we are the first of the believers": that is, they hoped that Allah would expiate their sins for them because they had preceded others in faith.

"That you travel by night with My servants" (أن أسر بعبادي): al-isra' means walking by night, and by "My servants" are meant the Children of Israel.

"Indeed you will be pursued" (إنكم متبعون): that is, by Pharaoh and his armies.

"A small band" (لشرذمة): that is, a group of people.

"Enraging us" (لغائظون): that is, doing what enrages and angers us.

"Cautious" (حذرون): that is, alert and prepared.

"And a noble station" (ومقام كريم): that is, a fine assembly that belonged to the princes and ministers.

"Thus" (كذلك): that is, our expulsion of them was in that manner, in that form.

"At sunrise" (مشرقين): that is, at the time of the sun's rising.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿They said, "No harm"﴾: this is the statement of the magicians to Pharaoh after he threatened and warned them. ﴿They said, "No harm"﴾: that is, there is no harm upon us from your cutting off our hands and feet and crucifying us. ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we will return﴾: that is, we will go back. Whatever you do to us, you are hastening our return to our Lord, and that is the thing we love most. And they said, ﴿Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins﴾: that is, our wrongdoings, ﴿that we were the first of the believers﴾ in this land in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.

After this great victory achieved by Moses and Aaron, the Exalted revealed to Moses, ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾: that is, walk with them at night, ﴿indeed you will be pursued﴾: that is, by Pharaoh and his soldiers. Pharaoh learned of Moses' determination to leave with the Children of Israel, so he sent into the cities, and he had hundreds of cities, ﴿gatherers﴾ of men: that is, assemblers, and it was as though a general mobilization. They said, inciting, ﴿Indeed, these are but a small band﴾: that is, Moses and the Children of Israel, whose members are few, ﴿and indeed they are enraging us﴾: that is, doing what enrages and angers us, ﴿and indeed we are all cautious﴾: that is, the government and the people are alert and prepared, so come to pursue them and return them to obedience. The Exalted hastened the good news in this report, so He said, ﴿So We expelled them﴾: that is, the family of Pharaoh, ﴿from gardens and springs and treasures﴾: that is, treasures of gold and silver that were buried beneath the earth, since the obliteration was on the currency, which became corrupt, whereas the stored gold and silver remained under the ground, since "treasure" applies to what is buried beneath the earth, though in the Law "treasure" is whatever its zakat has not been paid, whether beneath the earth or above it.

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Thus﴾: that is, our expulsion of them was thus, ﴿and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them﴾: that is, those blessings were inherited by the Children of Israel after the destruction of Pharaoh and all his soldiers. The words of the Exalted, ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾: that is, the family of Pharaoh pursued the Children of Israel at the time of sunrise, to overtake them and prevent them from leaving the land.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The strength of faith is a source of extraordinary courage, such that the believer rejoices in death because it brings him to his Lord.

2- Good hope in Allah and aspiring to His mercy, and the virtue of precedence in good.

3- The legitimacy of general mobilization and of adopting a special method in war that calms the fears of the nation, government and people alike.

4- The destruction of the wrongdoers and the annihilation of those who exceed limits in disbelief, evil and corruption.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Fa-lamma tara'a al-jam'an* (فلما تراءى الجمعان): meaning that each saw the other because they came close. The two hosts were the host of the Children of Israel and the host of Pharaoh.

*Inna lamudrakun* (إنا لمدركون): meaning that the companions of Musa from the Children of Israel said, "Indeed we will be overtaken," that is, Pharaoh and his soldiers will catch up with us.

*Qala kalla* (قال كلا): meaning that Musa, peace be upon him, said, "No!" That is, they will not overtake us and will not reach us.

*Fa-nfalaqa* (فانفلق): meaning it split open.

*Fa-kana kullu firqin ka-l-tawd* (فكان كل فرق كالطود): meaning each split part was like a mountain. The *tawd* (طود) is a mountain.

*Wa-azlafna thamma al-akharin* (وأزلفنا ثم الآخرين): meaning We brought the others near there, that is, Pharaoh and his soldiers.

*Inna fi dhalika la-ayah* (إن في ذلك لآية): meaning a lesson and an admonition that necessitates belief in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.

**The meaning of the verses:**

This is the end of the story of Musa, peace be upon him, with Pharaoh. Allah the Exalted says, explaining the end of the wrongdoers and the triumph of the believers:

﴿So when the two hosts saw each other﴾, the host of Musa and the host of Pharaoh, and they drew so close that each saw the other. ﴿The companions of Musa said﴾, that is, the Children of Israel, ﴿"Indeed, we are going to be overtaken!"﴾ That is, they became afraid when they saw Pharaoh's armies advancing toward them, and they cried out, "Indeed, we are going to be overtaken!" So Musa reassured them with his words, ﴿"No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me"﴾ to the way of my deliverance. Allah the Exalted says, ﴿So We revealed to Musa, "Strike the sea with your staff"﴾, that is, strike the sea with your staff. He struck it in obedience to the command of his Lord, and the sea split into two parts, each part of it like a great mountain. ﴿And We brought near the others there﴾, that is, We brought the others near there, namely Pharaoh and his armies. ﴿And We saved Musa and those with him, all of them﴾, that is, from the Children of Israel. ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾, the enemies of the Children of Israel, namely Pharaoh and his soldiers.

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed in that﴾, referring to the destruction of Pharaoh and the deliverance of Musa and the Children of Israel, ﴿is a sign﴾, that is, a clear mark that manifests the lordship, divinity, power, knowledge and mercy of Allah, and it is also a lesson and admonition for those who take heed. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾, O Muhammad, despite the cause and requirement of faith, because it had already preceded in the knowledge of Allah that they would not believe.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed your Lord, He is the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful﴾, that is, indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is the One who prevails over His command, who is not hindered in anything He wills, and whose purpose is not prevented, and who is merciful to His servants. So be patient in calling to Him, and put your trust in Him, for He is your helper and the one who humiliates your enemies.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The effects of enslavement are evident among the Children of Israel, manifested in their fear even while witnessing the signs.
2. The attribute of Allah's companionship is established in Musa's words, ﴿Indeed with me is my Lord﴾, for when He sent him He said to him, ﴿Indeed I am with you both﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46].
3. Divine revelation is established.
4. The sign of the splitting of the sea is among the greatest signs.
5. The prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) is confirmed by stories like these, which could not have been told except through special revelation.

*Fa-nazallu laha 'akifin*: That is, so we spend most of the day devoted to her worship.

*Qalu bal wajadna*: That is, they neither hear, nor benefit, nor harm. Rather, "We found our fathers worshipping them, so we are following them."

*Fa-innahum 'aduwwun li*: That is, they will be enemies to me on the Day of Resurrection if I worship them, because they will disown their worshippers.

*Illa Rabb al-'alamin*: Whoever worships Him will not be disowned by Him on the Day of Resurrection; rather, He will save him from the Fire and honor him with Paradise.

*Fa-huwa yahdin*: That is, to what will save me from punishment and make me happy in my worldly life and in the Hereafter.

*Wa-alladhi yumitni thumma yuhyin*: That is, He causes me to die when my term ends, then He revives me for the Day of Judgment.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

This is the beginning of the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Its purpose is to present the call of Ibrahim to the ears of the Quraysh, the people of Muhammad (ﷺ), so that they may take heed, believe, and affirm the oneness of God, and thus be saved from the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. God the Exalted says: ﴿And recite to them the news of Ibrahim﴾, that is, recite to your people from the Quraysh the account of Ibrahim at the time he said to his father and his people, ﴿"What do you worship?"﴾, questioning them so that he could respond to their answer. This is a wise method (*uslub hakim*, a wise approach) in calling to God and in teaching: he asks them and answers them based on the implication of their own question, which makes understanding easier and the acceptance of truth more likely.

﴿They said, "We worship idols"﴾, that is, in the form of statues, ﴿and we remain devoted to them﴾, that is, we spend most of the day devoted around them, seeking nearness to them and blessing (*tabarruk*, seeking blessing) through them, humbly submitting before them.

When he heard their answer, and they had spoken truthfully about it, he said to them, ﴿"Do they hear you when you call [on them]?"﴾, that is, when you call upon them, ﴿"or do they benefit you"﴾ if you ask benefit from them, ﴿"or do they harm [you]?"﴾ if you ask them to harm someone you want harmed? They answered, saying to all of that: No, no, no. ﴿Rather, we found our fathers doing thus﴾, so we did likewise, following them in imitation and adhering to their way.

At this point Ibrahim openly told them what he wanted them to understand, and said: ﴿"Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancient ones?"﴾, who are your grandfathers, from whom your fathers inherited this polytheism (*shirk*, associating partners with God) and falsehood. ﴿"Indeed, they are enemies to me"﴾, that is, enemies to me on the Day of Resurrection if I worship them along with you, because everything worshipped besides God will, on the Day of Resurrection, disown its worshippers and declare enmity toward them, seeking to save itself from the punishment of God. And His saying, ﴿"except the Lord of the worlds"﴾: He will not be an enemy to whoever worships Him, but rather will be loving to him and merciful toward him. Unquestionably, then, worship Him, O my people, and abandon the worship of those who will be enemies to you on the Day of Resurrection!

Then Ibrahim began to mention his Lord, praise Him, and glorify Him, making Him known and reminding those ignorant polytheists, and he said: ﴿"He who created me, and He guides me"﴾, that is, to the path of my salvation, my perfection, and my happiness, by making clear to me what He loves so that I may pursue it, and what He dislikes so that I may avoid it. ﴿"And He who feeds me and gives me drink"﴾, that is, He nourishes me with various kinds of food and gives me drink from what He created and made easy for me of various beverages: water, milk, and honey. ﴿"And when I am ill, it is He who cures me"﴾: when my body becomes sick and afflicted, it is He, and no other, who heals me. ﴿"And He who will cause me to die, then give me life"﴾, on the day He wills my death when the term He appointed for me, at which my life ends, has come, and then He will revive me on the Day of Resurrection and the raising. ﴿"And who I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense"﴾, that is, He will cover it and erase its trace from my soul on the Day of Recompense and Reckoning for the deeds of man in this world, for this is the abode of action and the Hereafter is the abode of recompense.

If it is asked: what is meant by the sin that Ibrahim mentioned for himself? The answer is that they are the three lies which Ibrahim told during his early life. The first was his saying: ﴿"Indeed, I am ill"﴾ [Al-Saffat: 89]. The second was: ﴿"Rather, this was done by their chief"﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 63]. The third was his saying to the tyrant: "She is my sister," and not "She is my wife." These are the lies that Ibrahim committed. He therefore feared them, and on the Day of Resurrection, when mankind asks him to intercede with their Lord, he will mention these lies and say, "I am not the one; go to Musa."

So let the believers take heed, for those who lie are not counted as many!

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 83–93:

Explanation of words:

"Rabbi hab li hukman" (My Lord, grant me wisdom): i.e., O Lord, bestow upon me, by Your grace, wisdom, meaning beneficial knowledge, and enable me to act upon it.

"Wa-alhiqni bil-salihin" (And join me with the righteous): that I may do their deeds in this world and be with them in the Hereafter.

"Wa-ij'al li lisana sidqin fil-akhirin" (And make for me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations): i.e., make for me a good remembrance by which I am mentioned among those who come after me.

"Wa-ghfir li abi" (And forgive my father): this was from him before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah.

"Wa la tukhzini yawma yub'athun" (And do not disgrace me on the day they are resurrected): i.e., do not expose me to shame.

"Bi-qalbin salim" (With a sound heart): i.e., free from polytheism (shirk) and hypocrisy (nifaq).

"Wa uzlifatil-jannatu" (And Paradise will be brought near): i.e., it will be brought close and made near for the God-fearing.

"Waburrizatil-jahimu lil-ghawin" (And Hellfire will be made apparent to the deviators): i.e., it will be displayed and made clearly visible to the deviators.

"Hal yansurunakum" (Can they help you?): i.e., by repelling the punishment from you.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the conclusion and end of the story of Ibrahim. When Ibrahim had admonished his people, he raised his hands to his Lord, asking and humbly imploring Him, and said: ﴿My Lord, grant me wisdom﴾, i.e., beneficial knowledge that prevents me from doing what would anger You against me and drives me to do what pleases You with me. ﴿And join me with the righteous﴾ in their good deeds in this world and in their companionship in Paradise. ﴿And make for me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations﴾, i.e., make for me a good remembrance by which I am mentioned among those of Your believing servants who come after me. ﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss﴾, who inherit it through faith and God-consciousness, after Your favor upon them and Your mercy toward them. ﴿And forgive my father, for he is among the misguided﴾, i.e., those ignorant of You and of what You love and what You dislike, so they did not worship You nor draw near to You. This request by Ibrahim was made before he knew that his father was an enemy of Allah, since that had been decreed for him from eternity; once he knew it, he disassociated himself from him. His saying ﴿And do not disgrace me﴾ means do not humiliate me ﴿on the day they are resurrected﴾, i.e., raised from their graves for reckoning and recompense for their deeds, ﴿the day when wealth and children will not benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾, i.e., but whoever comes to Allah, meaning comes to Him on the Day of Resurrection with a heart free from polytheism and hypocrisy. Such a person's righteous deeds will benefit him, since his heart is clear of what would nullify them, namely polytheism and disbelief, outward and inward. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near﴾, i.e., drawn near and made close to the God-fearing who fear their Lord and did not associate anything with Him in worship nor openly committed His disobedience. ﴿And Hellfire will be made apparent to the deviators﴾, i.e., displayed and raised up for those who were astray and misguided in this world, among the polytheists and those who excessively committed crime, evil and corruption. ﴿And it will be said to them﴾, i.e., they will be asked on the plains of resurrection: ﴿Where is what you used to worship besides Allah?﴾ Show them to us. ﴿Can they help you﴾ against what you are in, so that they repel the punishment from you? ﴿Or can they defend themselves﴾, so that they repel punishment from themselves if they are among the people of the Fire, because they were content to be worshipped and called people to worship them, like the devils and the criminals among mankind and jinn.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that Paradise is inherited, and God mentions the cause of its inheritance, which is God-consciousness, in His saying: ﴿That is the Garden which We cause to inherit from Our servants whoever was God-conscious﴾ [Maryam: 63].

2- The legitimacy of seeking forgiveness for one's parents if they died upon monotheism.

3- The invalidity of benefiting on the Day of Resurrection from anything other than faith and righteous deeds, after Allah's favor and mercy.

4- Encouragement toward God-consciousness and warning against deviation.

When Ibrahim had admonished his people, he raised his hands to his Lord, asking and humbly imploring Him, and said: ﴿My Lord, grant me wisdom﴾, i.e., beneficial knowledge that prevents me from doing what would anger You against me and drives me to do what pleases You with me. ﴿And join me with the righteous﴾ in their good deeds in this world and in their companionship in Paradise. ﴿And make for me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations﴾, i.e., make for me a good remembrance by which I am mentioned among those of Your believing servants who come after me. ﴿And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss﴾, who inherit it through faith and God-consciousness, after Your favor upon them and Your mercy toward them. ﴿And forgive my father, for he is among the misguided﴾, i.e., those ignorant of You and of what You love and what You dislike, so they did not worship You nor draw near to You. This request by Ibrahim was made before he knew that his father was an enemy of Allah, since that had been decreed for him from eternity; once he knew it, he disassociated himself from him. His saying ﴿And do not disgrace me﴾ means do not humiliate me ﴿on the day they are resurrected﴾, i.e., raised from their graves for reckoning and recompense for their deeds, ﴿the day when wealth and children will not benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾, i.e., but whoever comes to Allah, meaning comes to Him on the Day of Resurrection with a heart free from polytheism and hypocrisy. Such a person's righteous deeds will benefit him, since his heart is clear of what would nullify them, namely polytheism and disbelief, outward and inward. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near﴾, i.e., drawn near and made close to the God-fearing who fear their Lord and did not associate anything with Him in worship nor openly committed His disobedience. ﴿And Hellfire will be made apparent to the deviators﴾, i.e., displayed and raised up for those who were astray and misguided in this world, among the polytheists and those who excessively committed crime, evil and corruption. ﴿And it will be said to them﴾, i.e., they will be asked on the plains of resurrection: ﴿Where is what you used to worship besides Allah?﴾ Show them to us. ﴿Can they help you﴾ against what you are in, so that they repel the punishment from you? ﴿Or can they defend themselves﴾, so that they repel punishment from themselves if they are among the people of the Fire, because they were content to be worshipped and called people to worship them, like the devils and the criminals among mankind and jinn.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that Paradise is inherited, and God mentions the cause of its inheritance, which is God-consciousness, in His saying: ﴿That is the Garden which We cause to inherit from Our servants whoever was God-conscious﴾ [Maryam: 63].

2- The legitimacy of seeking forgiveness for one's parents if they died upon monotheism.

3- The invalidity of benefiting on the Day of Resurrection from anything other than faith and righteous deeds, after Allah's favor and mercy.

4- Encouragement toward God-consciousness and warning against deviation.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 83–93:

Explanation of words:

"Rabbi hab li hukman" (My Lord, grant me wisdom): i.e., O Lord, bestow upon me, by Your grace, wisdom, meaning beneficial knowledge, and enable me to act upon it.

"Wa-alhiqni bil-salihin" (And join me with the righteous): that I may do their deeds in this world and be with them in the Hereafter.

"Wa-ij'al li lisana sidqin fil-akhirin" (And make for me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations): i.e., make for me a good remembrance by which I am mentioned among those who come after me.

"Wa-ghfir li abi" (And forgive my father): this was from him before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah.

"Wa la tukhzini yawma yub'athun" (And do not disgrace me on the day they are resurrected): i.e., do not expose me to shame.

"Bi-qalbin salim" (With a sound heart): i.e., free from polytheism (shirk) and hypocrisy (nifaq).

"Wa uzlifatil-jannatu" (And Paradise will be brought near): i.e., it will be brought close and made near for the God-fearing.

"Waburrizatil-jahimu lil-ghawin" (And Hellfire will be made apparent to the deviators): i.e., it will be displayed and made clearly visible to the deviators.

"Hal yansurunakum" (Can they help you?): i.e., by repelling the punishment from you.

Explanation of the Words:

"Fa-kubkibu fīhā" (so they were hurled headlong into it): that is, they were thrown on their faces into Hell and tumbled within it until they reached its bottom.

"Al-ghāwūn" (the misguided): the plural of ghāwin, meaning one whose heart is corrupt and whose soul is defiled by shirk and sins.

"Junūd Iblīs" (the hosts of Iblis): that is, his followers, supporters and helpers, from among mankind and the jinn.

"Idh nusawwīkum bi-Rabb al-ʿālamīn" (when we made you equal to the Lord of the worlds): that is, in worship, so we worshipped you as Allah, exalted is He, is worshipped.

"Wa-lā ṣadīqin ḥamīm" (nor a close friend): that is, one who cares about our affairs and whose friendship benefits us, one we might take refuge in from being punished.

"Fa-law anna lanā karrah" (if only we had a return): that is, a return to the world so that we might believe, affirm Allah's oneness, and worship our Lord in the manner He has prescribed for us.

Meaning of the Verses:

Concerning the Almighty's words, ﴿So they were hurled headlong into it﴾, following that reproachful and rebuking question mentioned in His words, ﴿And it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to worship besides Allah? Can they help you or defend themselves?"﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 92–93], they failed to answer, since it was impossible for them to do so. Allah, exalted is He, then informed about them that they were hurled headlong into Hell, that is, they were thrown upon their faces and tumbled within it, they and the misguided ones (al-ghawun), the plural of ghawin, meaning one whose creed and deeds are corrupt, and all the hosts of Iblis, the followers of Satan and his helpers, the callers to shirk, sin and crime upon the earth, from among mankind and the jinn.

The Almighty's words, ﴿They will say, while they are disputing therein﴾, meaning: while they are in Hell disputing, each one placing the responsibility and blame upon the other. The polytheists said to those they had associated with Allah, ﴿By Allah, we were certainly in clear error﴾, meaning manifest and evident, not open to dispute, ﴿when we made you equal to the Lord of the worlds﴾, the Mighty and Majestic, so we worshipped you alongside Him. ﴿And none led us astray except the criminals﴾, who are the callers to shirk, evil and misguidance, who committed crimes against themselves and corrupted them, and committed crimes against us, corrupting our souls through shirk and sins.

The Almighty's words, ﴿So we have no intercessors, nor any close friend﴾, are also their statement, in which they affirmed another fact: that on this Day they have no intercessors who will intercede for them with Allah, neither from the angels nor from mankind and the jinn, since no intercession benefits one who dies in shirk and disbelief. Their words, "nor any close friend," mean that they have no close friend whose friendship and allegiance would benefit them.

Then, after despairing of finding any intercessors, they said wishfully, ﴿If only we had a return﴾, that is, a return to the abode of the world, ﴿so that we might be among the believers﴾, so that we would believe, affirm Allah's oneness, and follow the Messengers. This is the last of what Allah, exalted is He, related of their speech in Hell.

The Almighty's words, ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, that is, in what has been mentioned of the hurling headlong of the polytheists, the misguided ones, and all the hosts of Iblis into Hell, their disputing there, what they said and wished for, their deprivation of intercession, and their eternal abiding in the Fire, ﴿a sign﴾, that is, a lesson for whoever takes heed from others. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾, meaning most of your people, O our Messenger, were not believers; otherwise they would have benefited from these lessons, believed, affirmed Allah's oneness, and submitted. ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾, that is, the One who prevails over His affair, does what He wills and decides what He desires, the Merciful to His servants, who, if they turn back to Him and devote worship to Him sincerely, He honors in His neighborhood, in the Gardens of Bliss.

Guidance from the Verses:

1. Affirmation that the callers to fornication, usury, superstition and shirk among mankind are among the hosts of Iblis.

2. Affirmation that the criminals are those who corrupt their own souls and the souls of others by calling them to misguidance, and who drive them toward sins.

3. Affirmation that intercession will not be for those who die in shirk and disbelief.

4. Lessons, admonitions and signs do not benefit in guiding a people whose wretchedness Allah has decreed from eternity and whom He knew would not believe, so He wrote this upon them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 116–122:

Explanation of the words:

*"La-in lam tanta"* (If you do not desist): That is, from calling us to abandon our gods and to worship your God alone.

*"Min al-marjumin"* (Among those stoned): That is, those killed by being pelted with stones.

*"Fa-ftah bayni wa-baynahum fath'an"* (Judge between me and them with a judgment): That is, decide between me and them with a decision by which You destroy them and deliver me and those believers who are with me.

*"Fi al-fulk al-mashhun"* (In the laden ship): That is, the ship filled with passengers and pairs of the other created beings.

*"Ba'da al-baqin"* (Afterward, the rest): That is, after We delivered Noah and the believers by their boarding the ship, We drowned the disbelievers, since their drowning came after the deliverance of the believers.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the dialogue between Noah and his people. When he called them to monotheism, repeated the call to them, silenced them on many occasions, and their proofs were exhausted, they resorted to threats and warnings. This is what God related about them in His saying, ﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned"﴾. That is, by oath of our gods, if you do not desist, O Noah, from belittling us, reviling our gods, and demanding that we abandon their worship, ﴿you will surely be among those stoned﴾, meaning we will surely kill you by pelting you with stones. Here, after a call that lasted nine hundred and fifty years, Noah raised his complaint to God, saying: ﴿My Lord, indeed my people have denied me. So judge between me and them with a judgment﴾, meaning judge between us and decide the matter of our coexistence with one another, so destroy them ﴿and deliver me and those believers who are with me﴾. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We delivered him and those with him in the laden ship﴾, meaning filled with various kinds of animals. ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward﴾, meaning after We delivered Noah and those with him among the believers by their boarding the ship. The water kept rising, both what descended from the sky and what gushed from the earth, until everyone on the earth and the mountains drowned, and no one was saved except Noah and the people of the ship. God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, meaning a lesson, from the mentioned struggle between monotheism and polytheism, and in the outcome of monotheism, which is the deliverance of its adherents, and of polytheism, which is the destruction of its adherents. ﴿But most of them were not believers﴾. But the people of Makkah did not take heed. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾ because of what had already been decreed in God's knowledge of their non-belief. So do not grieve over them. ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful﴾, O noble Messenger, He alone and none other, the Exalted in Might, the Victorious, the Merciful toward whoever of His servants repents, for He does not punish him but shows mercy to him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The clarification of the way of wrongdoers and tyrants: when proofs fail them, they resort to force.

2- The permissibility of seeking help from God and asking for a decisive judgment between the oppressed and the oppressors.

3- God's swift response to His servant Noah, because of his patience over many centuries. When his patience ran out and he raised his complaint to his Lord, He answered him immediately, delivering him and destroying his enemies.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 26, verses 123–131**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Kadhdhabat 'Aad:* 'Aad was the name of the tribe's forefather, and the tribe was named after him.

*Akhuhum Hud:* Their brother in lineage.

*Fattaqu Allah:* That is, fear His punishment, so do not associate anything with Him.

*Atabnoona bi-kulli rey'in:* That is, a high, elevated place.

*Aayah:* That is, a lofty, well-built, towering palace.

*Ta'batheon:* That is, in your buildings, where you build what you will not dwell in.

*Wa-tattakhidhuna masani':* That is, impregnable fortresses and lofty palaces.

*La'allakum takhludun:* That is, as if you hope for and expect to live forever on the earth.

*Wa-idha batashtum:* That is, when you seize someone, you attack them with violence and harshness.

*Jabbarin:* That is, tyrannical oppressors.

**The meaning of the verses:**

This is the beginning of the account of Hud, peace be upon him. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿The people of 'Aad denied the messengers﴾, that is, the tribe of 'Aad denied the Messenger Hud. ﴿When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾, that is, will you not fear Allah's punishment by abandoning shirk and sins? The meaning is: fear Allah, your Lord, and do not associate anything with Him. His words ﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾ inform them that he is a messenger of Allah to them, conveying to them His command and prohibition, and that he is trustworthy in this, neither adding to nor subtracting from what his Lord commanded him to convey to them. Accordingly, ﴿so fear Allah and obey me﴾, that is, by virtue of my being a messenger sent to you, for my obedience is obligatory upon you until I convey to you what I was sent with.

His words ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾, that is, for conveying my message to you, any reward whatsoever. And had he said, "My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds," this would mean: my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds, glorified and exalted is He, since it is He who sent me and charged me, and it is He whom I hope will reward me for bearing my message to you and conveying it to you. Accordingly, ﴿so fear Allah﴾, that is, fear His punishment by abandoning shirk and sins, ﴿and obey me﴾ by accepting what I convey to you, so that you may be perfected and attain happiness.

His words: ﴿Do you build on every high place a landmark, wasting your time?﴾ Hud rebukes his people for their absorption in this world, their preoccupation with what is of no concern, and their neglect of what concerns them. He says to them, as one who denounces them: ﴿Do you build on every high place﴾, that is, a lofty, elevated place, ﴿a landmark﴾, that is, a palace built to tower high. ﴿Wasting your time﴾, in that you build where you will not dwell, so it is merely for amusement and idle play. His words ﴿and make for yourselves reservoirs﴾, which are high structures like fortresses, or water cisterns, or fortresses ﴿so that you may live forever﴾, that is, as if you might live forever. But you are not immortal; your stay in them is brief. His words ﴿And when you seize, you seize like tyrants﴾, that is, when you overpower anyone, you overpower them like cruel tyrants, seizing them with violence and harshness, without mercy or gentleness. ﴿So fear Allah﴾, O my people, ﴿and fear His punishment and painful torment﴾, ﴿and obey me﴾ in what I call you to and convey to you from my Lord, for that is better for you than turning away and persisting in falsehood.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Commanding piety is sincere counsel to the one commanded, because salvation and success are not complete for the servant except through it.
2. Messengers are trustworthy in what they carry and in what they convey to people.
3. Taking payment for explaining the Shari'ah and calling to it is prohibited.
4. The servant should not be extravagant, building what he will not live in and storing what he will not eat.
5. Harshness and severity in seizing and in holding people accountable are to be condemned.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 132–140:

Explanation of the words:

Amaddakum (أمدكم): He bestowed upon you, granting you favours.

Bi-an'am (بأنعام): camels, cattle and sheep.

Adhab yawm 'azim (عذاب يوم عظيم): it is the day of their destruction in this world and the day of their resurrection on the Day of Judgement.

Sawa'un 'alayna (سواء علينا): it is equal to us whether you admonish us or do not admonish us, for we will not obey you.

Inna hadha illa khuluq al-awwalin (إن هذا إلا خلق الأولين): what you admonish us about, such as building and other things, is nothing but the custom and habit of the earlier people, so we follow their way, and we will not be punished.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the dialogue that took place between the Prophet of Allah, Hud (عليه السلام), and his polytheistic people, when he commanded them to be mindful of Allah and to obey him, and also commanded them to be mindful of Allah, who had granted them increase (amadd), that is, who had bestowed upon them the kinds of blessings that they know. For obedience to the Bestower is gratitude for His bounty, and disobedience to Him is ingratitude for His bounty. So He said: ﴿And fear Him who has aided you with what you know﴾, and He explained this with His words: ﴿He has aided you with cattle﴾, that is, livestock of camels, cattle and sheep; ﴿and sons﴾, that is, male and female children; ﴿and gardens﴾, that is, orchards; ﴿and springs﴾ for their irrigation, for your watering and for your purification. Then he said to them, out of compassion for them: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day﴾, if you persist in polytheism and sins. It may be a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter. They were punished in this world by their destruction, and they will be punished in the Hereafter because they died as disbelievers, polytheists, disobedient and criminal. This is what their Prophet Hud (عليه السلام) admonished them with. Their response to his admonition was what Allah, the Exalted, reported in His words: ﴿They said: "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers."﴾ That is, it is equal to us whether your admonition, that is, your warning and reminder, exists or not, so we will not abandon our gods because of your words, and we will not believe in you. And they said: ﴿This is nothing but the custom of the earlier people﴾, referring to what we are upon of building and monumental construction and worship of our gods, ﴿this is nothing but the custom of the earlier people﴾, that is, the practice and habit of those who came before us among mankind, and we will not be punished for it.

Allah, the Exalted, said, informing about the outcome of that dialogue and that call undertaken by the Prophet of Allah, Hud: ﴿So they denied him﴾, that is, they denied Hud regarding what he brought them, what he called them to, and what he warned them against. ﴿So We destroyed them﴾, that is, by their denial and their aversion. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾ of the destruction of those who denied, a lesson for your people, O Muhammad, if they would take heed. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾, because of what had already preceded in Allah's knowledge of their not believing, and therefore admonitions and lessons did not benefit them. ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾: He seized the tyrannical, obstinate ones, sent down His vengeance upon them, and made them taste the bitterness of His punishment; and He showed mercy to His allies, saved them, and destroyed their enemies.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Varying the methods of da'wah, and reminding the deniers of what is perceptible and visible to them.

2- Warning of Allah's punishment and cautioning against the consequences of disobedience are among the methods of da'wah.

3- Explaining the way of people in imitating and following their forefathers, even if they were misguided and ignorant.

4- Establishing monotheism (tawhid), prophethood and resurrection, for this is the purpose of these narratives.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*"Thamud denied the messengers"*: i.e., the tribe of Thamud denied their prophet Salih.

*"In what you have here, secure"*: i.e., among the good things and blessings, fearing no one.

*"Its spathe is soft"*: i.e., the spathe (flower cluster) of the date palm is tender and delicate as long as it is within its *kufra* (the sheath or covering that encloses it).

*"Hewing out houses from the mountains"*: i.e., you cut the rock in the mountain with carving tools and make houses from it.

*"Exultant"*: i.e., skilled in the craft, and also proud, arrogant, and deluded by their own handiwork.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 153–159:

Explanation of the words:

"إنما أنت من المسحرين" (You are only one of those who are bewitched): those who have been enchanted, and whose enchantment has been exaggerated until it overpowered their minds.

"فأت بآية إن كنت من الصادقين" (So bring a sign, if you are among the truthful): if you are truthful that you are a messenger, then bring us a sign that proves it.

"لها شرب ولكم شرب يوم معلوم" (For her is a share of water, and for you is a share on a known day): that is, one day she drinks from the spring, and for you there is another known day.

"فعقروها فأصبحوا نادمين" (Then they hamstrung her, and they became regretful): that is, they did not believe, so they killed her, and in the morning they were regretful when they witnessed the punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the dialogue between Salih (peace be upon him) and his people, Thamud. When he reminded them and admonished them, they responded with what Allah, the Exalted, related about them in His words: ﴿They said: "You are only one of those who are bewitched."﴾ That is, those who have been enchanted, and whose enchantment has been exaggerated until it overpowered their minds, so they do not know what they say. ﴿"You are only a human like us"﴾ who eats food and drinks drink; you are neither a lord nor an angel, so we should submit to you and obey you. ﴿"So bring a sign"﴾ a strong proof and a truthful evidence showing that you are truly the Messenger of Allah, and that you are among the truthful messengers. Salih answered them with what Allah, the Exalted, related in His words: ﴿He said: "This is a she-camel"﴾, that is, of great size. He asked his Lord for a sign, and He gave him this she-camel. He continued standing, praying and supplicating while they watched, until the mountain split open and this she-camel, the great sign, came out of it. So he said: ﴿"This is a she-camel; she has a share of water"﴾, that is, a portion and allotment of the town's water which she drinks alone, with no one coming to drink with her, ﴿"and for you is a share on a known day, which you alone shall drink."﴾ He warned them not to touch her with harm, neither by striking, nor by killing, nor by preventing her from drinking, ﴿"for a painful punishment will seize you on a great day."﴾ Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then they hamstrung her﴾, that is, they denied him and disobeyed him, and hamstrung her by striking her in her forelegs and hind legs, so she fell down, and they killed her. When they hamstrung her, Salih said to them: ﴿"Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied."﴾ [Hud: 65] So they became regretful because of that. On the morning of the third day, the Cry seized them at sunrise, and they were all destroyed, while Allah the Exalted saved Salih and those who believed with him. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, that is, a great sign of Allah's power, His knowledge, and that He alone deserves worship. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾ despite the clarity of the evidence, because faith had not preceded for them in Allah's decree and destiny. ﴿And indeed, your Lord﴾, O Messenger, ﴿He is the Exalted in Might, the Victorious who cannot be overcome, the Merciful to His allies and righteous servants.﴾

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation that magic is a human practice, known to people and practiced since ancient times.

2- The custom of people demanding signs when they are called to the true religion.

3- The existence of signs does not necessarily entail the faith of those who demand them; rather, most of them do not believe.

4- Regret is part of repentance, but neither regret nor repentance benefits at the moment of witnessing the punishment or its signs.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 160–166:

Explanation of the vocabulary:

Qawm Lut (the people of Lut): they are the inhabitants of the cities of Sodom (Sadum) and Gomorrah (Amuriyah) and other villages. Lut is the Prophet of Allah, Lut son of Haran, the nephew of Ibrahim.

Akhuhum Lut (their brother Lut): this is a brotherhood of land and residence, not a brotherhood of lineage or religion.

Inni lakum rasul amin (indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you): that is, I am sent to you and not to others, and I am trustworthy in conveying my message, so I neither diminish nor add to it.

Fattaqu Allah (so fear Allah): by believing in Him, worshipping Him alone, and abandoning His acts of disobedience.

Wa ma as'alukum 'alayhi (and I do not ask you any wage for it): that is, for the conveying of the message, no payment in return for my guidance and teaching of you.

Ata'tun al-dhukran min al-'alamin (do you approach males from among the worlds?): that is, do you commit the abomination with men and leave the women?

Bal antum qawm 'adun (rather, you are a people who transgress): that is, you are aggressors, wrongdoers, exceeding the limit in excess of evil.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the account of Lut with his people, the companions of the overturned cities. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The people of Lut denied the messengers﴾. That is, they denied Lut the Messenger, and his denial is considered a denial of all the messengers, because the call of Allah is one. They denied him when he called them to worship Allah alone and to abandon abominations, wrongdoing, evil and corruption. Their brother Lut said to them: this is a brotherhood of homeland and nothing more, for Lut was from the land of Babylon by origin, his religion was Islam, and his father Haran was the brother of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. When Lut was sent to the people of this land and lived among them, he was called their brother by virtue of companionship and the shared homeland. ﴿Will you not fear Allah?﴾ He commanded them to the fear of Allah and urged them toward it, because they were persisting in grave sins, so he feared destruction for them and called them to the means of salvation, which is the fear of Allah the Exalted through obedience to Him and abandoning His acts of disobedience. He said to them: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾, so do not doubt my message, and obey me. And I do not ask you for any wage for conveying my message to you; my wage I take from the Lord of the worlds, who entrusted me with this message and commanded me to convey it to you. Here he denounced their greatest evil, saying, rebuking and reproaching them: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds﴾, committing the abomination with them, ﴿and leave﴾, that is, you abandon what Allah created for you of your spouses. ﴿Rather, you are a people who transgress﴾, that is, you exceed the limits drawn by the Sharia, reason and human nature.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The permissibility of using the term brotherhood of homeland without religion or lineage.

2- Trustworthiness is a requirement of prophethood, for every messenger says: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾.

3- The path to salvation of the individual and the community lies in the fear of Allah the Exalted and obedience to the Messenger ﷺ.

4- It is obligatory to denounce evil and to condemn it in its perpetrator, perhaps he will refrain.

5- The greatest abomination committed on earth is the abomination of sodomy (liwat). We seek refuge in Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 167–175:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Surely, if you do not desist⦆ (la-in lam tantahi): that is, from your denouncing of what we commit of the obscenity.

﴿From those expelled⦆ (min al-mukhrajin): that is, from our lands, and your being driven out from our homes.

﴿Of those who hate your deed⦆ (min al-qalin): that is, those who hate it with intense hatred.

﴿My Lord, deliver me and my family from what they do⦆: that is, from the punishment and torment of what they do of obscenities.

﴿So We delivered him and his family⦆: that is, We delivered Lot, who called upon Us, and his family, namely his believing wife and his two daughters.

﴿Except an old woman who was among those who remained behind⦆: that is, We did not deliver her, since We had decreed her destruction along with the wrongdoers, so We left her with them until she perished among them, because she was a disbeliever and content with the deed of the people.

﴿And We rained upon them a rain⦆: that is, He sent down upon them stones from the sky, so they were rained upon with them after the lands were overturned, its highest part made lowest.

﴿And evil was the rain of those who were warned⦆: that is, wretched was the rain upon those who were warned, for they did not comply, and they did not refrain from evil and corruption.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues with what passed between the Prophet of God, Lot, and his criminal people. When he admonished them, advised them, commanded them and forbade them, and they heard all of that from him, they answered with what God related about them: ﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled."⦆ That is, if you do not desist from denouncing our committing of the obscenity, we will expel you from our lands and drive you out from among us, and you will not remain with us for a single hour. Be warned, O man! Then Lot, the Messenger, peace be upon him, answered them with his words: ﴿"I am, of your deed, one of those who hate it."⦆ That is, I am among those who hate your committing of the obscenity with the utmost hatred. Then he turned to his Lord, calling and humbly beseeching, and said: ﴿"My Lord, deliver me and my family from what they do."⦆ This was after he had remained calling them and enduring for many years, and he found no choice but to flee to his Lord to rescue him from them, so he said: ﴿"My Lord, deliver me and my family"⦆ from the punishment and torment of what they do of committing the obscenity, of the worlds. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We delivered him and his family⦆, namely his Muslim wife and his two Muslim daughters, naturally. ﴿Except an old woman⦆, namely his disbelieving wife, who colluded with the wrongdoers and was content with the abominable act, was among those who remained behind, that is, those left behind after Lot's departure from the land, so that she would perish with those who perished. God the Exalted said: ﴿Then We destroyed the others⦆, that is, after We had delivered Lot and all his family with the exception of the disbelieving old woman, We destroyed, that is, We annihilated, the others. ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned⦆: after overturning the lands, its highest part made lowest, He rained upon them a rain of stones from the sky, to strike whoever was outside the overturned, inverted cities.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign⦆: that is, in what we have mentioned of the destruction of the deniers, the extravagant and the wrongdoers, there is a great sign and proof for whoever hears and sees. ﴿And most of them were not believers⦆: because it had preceded in God the Exalted's knowledge that they would not believe. So glory be to God, the Mighty. And His saying: ﴿And indeed your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful⦆: and indeed your Lord, O our Messenger, He, and none other, is the Mighty, the Victorious, the Subduer of all wrongdoers and the extravagant, the Merciful to His allies and His believing servants.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Threatening with expulsion is an ancient human practice.

2- The obligation to hate evil and corruption in every form.

3- The answering of the supplication of the wronged, especially if he is one of the righteous.

4- The expectation of punishment when evil spreads and injustice and corruption grow great.

5- Signs, however great they are, do not necessarily entail faith and obedience.

6- Whoever has not already been granted faith will not believe, even if every sign is brought to him.

7- Manifestations of God's power, knowledge and mercy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 185–191:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Innama anta min al-musahharin﴾ (ﷺ): i.e., among those who eat food and drink, so you are not a king to be obeyed.

﴿Wa in nazunnuka la-min al-kadhibin﴾: i.e., we do not consider you to be anything but one of the liars.

﴿Fa-asqit alayna kisafan﴾: i.e., pieces of the sky, with which you would destroy us, if you are truthful in what you say.

﴿Adhab yawm al-zullah﴾: i.e., the cloud that overshadowed them, then blazed upon them as fire.

﴿Inna fi dhalika la-ayah﴾: i.e., indeed there is in that a lesson and a sign for whoever takes heed, and a sign indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ).

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the story of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) and the people of al-Aykah and the people of Madyan. When he admonished and exhorted them, their answer was what Allah, the Exalted, related about them in His words ﴿They said: "You are only one of those who have been bewitched"﴾, i.e., O Shu'ayb, ﴿of those who have been bewitched﴾, whose minds magic has overcome, so they do not know what they do or say. Just as you are a human like us who eats food and drinks drink, you are not an angel-king whom we should obey. ﴿And we do not think you are anything but a liar﴾, i.e., we think you are no more than one of the liars among men. ﴿So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us﴾, i.e., pieces of the sky with which You destroy us ﴿if you are of the truthful﴾ in your claim that you are a messenger of Allah to us. He answered them, saying what Allah, the Exalted, mentioned: ﴿My Lord knows best what you do﴾, and the implication of this is that He will recompense you for your deeds. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But they denied him﴾ in everything he brought them, and thereby deserved the punishment. ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, sent upon them an intense heat by which the atmosphere blazed, or nearly so. They sought refuge in their dwellings, caves and underground cellars, but these did not avail them anything. Then a cloud formed in the sky of their land, and some of them went to it and found it to be cool breeze, cold and pleasant. They called out to the people: "Come!" They came, and when they had all gathered beneath it, it turned into fire and burned them, and the earth shook beneath them, and they perished to the last one.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, i.e., a sign for your people, O Muhammad, of Our power, Our knowledge, the obligation of worshipping Us, and the truthfulness of Our messenger. ﴿But most of them are not believers﴾, because it had already been decreed in Our knowledge that they would not believe. ﴿And indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is the Mighty, i.e., the Overpowering over His affair, the Merciful toward whoever of His servants repents.﴾

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- This is the end of seven stories mentioned concisely, as consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ) and a warning to the polytheist deniers.

2- The call of the messengers is one, and their method is almost one: commanding the fear of Allah and obedience to His messenger.

3- It is a practice that people give as an excuse that the messenger should not be a human, and therefore they do not believe.

4- Demanding signs is almost a consistent practice, and few believe in spite of them.

5- Affirmation of monotheism, prophethood, and resurrection, which is the fruit of every story recounted in this Great Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 192–201:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾: that is, the Noble Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.

﴿The Trustworthy Spirit﴾: Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, the trustworthy one over the revelation of Allah the Exalted.

﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾: that is, the books of the former peoples. The singular of zubur (scriptures) is zubra, like ṣaḥifa (page) and ṣuḥuf.

﴿Is it not a sign for them﴾: that is, an indication and proof by which the Children of Israel knew it.

﴿Upon some of the non-Arabs﴾: the a'jamī (non-Arab) is one who cannot speak Arabic.

﴿Thus We have inserted it﴾: that is, disbelief into the hearts of the criminals among the disbelievers of Makkah.

The meaning of the verses:

The disbelievers of Makkah denied that the Qur'an is a revelation that Allah the Exalted sent down, and by this they denied that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. From here they rejected everything he brought them of monotheism and other matters. The recitation of these narratives by Muhammad (ﷺ), who neither reads nor writes, is a definite proof that it is a divine revelation sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), and that by this he is His Messenger. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And indeed it﴾, that is, the Qur'an which the polytheists denied, ﴿is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾, Jibril, peace be upon him, ﴿upon your heart﴾, that is, the Messenger, because the heart is what receives revelation, since it is the seat of perception, awareness and memorization. His saying, ﴿that you may be among the warners﴾, explains the reason for the Qur'an being sent down to him, and by it he became one of the warning Messengers. His saying, ﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾, that is, the Qur'an is mentioned in the divine books that preceded it, such as the Torah and the Gospel. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Is it not a sign for them﴾, that is, for the Quraysh disbelievers, ﴿a sign﴾, that is, an indication that the Qur'an is the revelation and Book of Allah, and that Muhammad is the servant and Messenger of Allah, ﴿that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it﴾, that is, the Children of Israel knew it, such as ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, who said: "By Allah, I know that Muhammad is a Messenger more than I know that so-and-so is my son, for it is possible that my son's mother has betrayed me, but Muhammad cannot be other than the Messenger of Allah." Concerning them the Exalted said, ﴿They recognize it as they recognize their own sons﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:146; al-An'am 6:20]. Whoever recognizes Muhammad as a Messenger recognizes the Qur'an as a divine revelation.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾, that is, in clear Arabic, and it had been recited to them by a non-Arab, ﴿they would not have believed in it﴾, that is, out of arrogance and zealotry, saying: "A non-Arab and an Arab?" His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Thus We have inserted it﴾, that is, denial and non-belief, ﴿into the hearts of the criminals﴾, that is, just as We inserted denial into the hearts of the criminals, if a non-Arab recited the Qur'an to them, We would insert denial into the hearts of the criminals if Muhammad (ﷺ) recited it to them. The reason for this is that transgression against oneself through committing grave sins naturally prevents the soul from accepting the truth, because of the sins that have covered it (ran) and the wrongdoings that have surrounded it. His saying, ﴿They do not believe in it﴾, is an emphasis on the negation of belief, until they see the painful punishment, that is, their denial of the Qur'an and of the one to whom it was sent down will continue until they see the painful torment; at that time their belief will not benefit them, and they will not be given respite.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the belief in divine revelation and Muhammadan prophethood.

2- Explanation that Jibril is the one who used to bring the Qur'anic revelation down upon the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

3- Affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood and that Muhammad is among the warners.

4- Explanation that the Qur'an is mentioned in the earlier scriptures, by the testimony of the scholars of the People of the Book.

5- When the effects of sins and crimes accumulate upon the soul, they block it from repentance and prevent it from belief.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 202–212:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Hal nahnu munzarun* (هل نحن منظرون): i.e., will we be given respite so that we may believe? The answer is decisively: No, no.

*Afara'ayt* (أفرأيت): i.e., tell me.

*In matta'nahum sinin* (إن متعناهم سنين): i.e., We let them remain alive, eating, drinking and marrying.

*Ma kanu yu'adun* (ما كانوا يوعدون): i.e., of the punishment.

*Ma aghna 'anhum* (ما أغنى عنهم): i.e., what availed them that long enjoyment, neither in averting the punishment nor in lightening it?

*Illa laha munzirun* (إلا لها منذرون): i.e., messengers who warned its people of the consequence of disbelief and polytheism.

*Dhikra* (ذكرى): i.e., admonition.

*Wa ma tanazzalat bihi al-shayatin* (وما تنزلت به الشياطين): i.e., it is not possible for them, nor proper for them, that they should descend with it.

*Wa ma yastati'un* (وما يستطيعون): i.e., they are not able.

*Innahum 'an al-sam'* (إنهم عن السمع): i.e., from hearing the speech of the angels, they are removed.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues to establish Muhammadan prophethood and to affirm revelation. The context has stated that the criminals will not believe in this Qur'an until they see the painful punishment. It will come upon them suddenly (*baghtatan*), i.e., unexpectedly, while they do not perceive (*la yash'uran*), i.e., do not know of it until it overtakes them. Then they will say: ﴿Will we be given respite?﴾ i.e., they will wish that they were granted time so that they might believe and set right what they corrupted.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then do they seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ when they said to the Messenger, "We will not believe in you until you cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us" (i.e., decisively), are they foolish or insane, seeking to hasten the punishment of God which, if it came upon them, would be their destruction, all of them? Then He said to His Messenger: ﴿Have you considered?﴾ O Our Messenger, ﴿if We let them enjoy for years﴾ by prolonging their lives and widening their provisions, so that they lived many years, and then Our punishment came upon them, i.e., tell me: would that enjoyment avail them anything? ﴿What they were enjoying did not avail them﴾, i.e., it did not avail them anything, neither in averting the punishment, nor in delaying it, nor in lightening it.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not destroy any town﴾ like those towns whose mention has passed in this surah ﴿except that it had warners﴾, i.e., it had messengers who warned its people of God's punishment if they persisted in polytheism, disbelief, evil and corruption. And His saying ﴿a reminder﴾, i.e., an admonition, so that perhaps they would be admonished. And His saying ﴿And We were not unjust﴾ in destroying those whom We destroyed after We had warned them.

It was revealed in response to the polytheistic criminals who said that the devils cast the Qur'an upon the tongue of Muhammad, just as they bring the news of the heavens to soothsayers. ﴿The devils did not bring it down﴾ as the deniers claim ﴿nor is it proper for them﴾, i.e., it is not fitting for the devils, nor is it possible for them, to do that, because they are removed from hearing, i.e., from hearing the speech of the angels, since God, exalted is He, stationed meteors which barred them from hearing from the heaven. Therefore the claim of the polytheists is void from its foundation.

**Guidance of the verses:**

Among the guidance of these verses:

1. Clarification that when the criminals witness the punishment, they wish for repentance, and it is not granted to them.

2. Clarification that hastening the punishment of God is foolishness, a misjudgment in opinion and corruption of intellect.

3. Clarification that long life and abundant provision do not avail their possessor anything of God's punishment when it descends upon him.

4. Clarification of God's way, that He does not destroy a community except after warning and clarification.

5. Refutation of the claims of the polytheists that the Qur'an is of the same kind as what the soothsayers say, and that the devils descend with it.
