Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 213–220:

Explanation of the words:

﴿So do not invoke another god along with Allah, lest you be among those punished﴾: that is, do not worship another god alongside Allah, because du'a (supplication, invocation) is worship.

﴿And warn your closest kin﴾: they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib.

﴿And lower your wing﴾: that is, be gentle toward them.

﴿But if they disobey you﴾: that is, they refuse to accept your call to monotheism (tawhid) and reject what you call them to.

﴿Then say, "Indeed, I am free of what you do"﴾: that is, free of worshipping other than Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾: that is, to prayer, so you pray at night (tahajjud) alone.

﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾: that is, He sees your movements among the worshippers as you bow, prostrate and stand.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in seeking the guidance of Quraysh, the people of Muhammad ﷺ. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So do not invoke another god along with Allah, lest you be among those punished﴾, contains a clear allusion and indication that it is a rebuke to the polytheists who invoke idols as gods. It is a call that wakes them from their slumber: if the Messenger of Allah is forbidden to worship other than Allah, and would be punished among the punished if he did, then others are all the more so. The speech thus runs in the manner of "It is you I mean, but listen, O neighbour!" 

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And warn your closest kin﴾, is a command from Allah to His Messenger to first single out his relatives with his warning, since they are most entitled to seek their salvation from punishment. The Messenger carried out his Lord's command. It is reported in the Sahihs from Abu Hurayah (may Allah be pleased with him) that when the verse ﴿And warn your closest kin﴾ was revealed to him, he (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase yourselves from Allah (meaning by faith and righteous deeds after abandoning polytheism and sins), for I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah, that is, against His punishment. O 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, ask me from my wealth whatever you wish; I cannot avail you anything against Allah."

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers﴾, is a command for him to be gentle toward the believers, to show them compassion and kindness, and to be pleasant to them, so that faith may take firm root in their hearts and they may be safe from the peril of apostasy, which might befall them if they were treated harshly and severely while they were at the beginning of the path to Allah, exalted is He.

His saying ﴿But if they disobey you﴾ means: those whom you have been commanded to call to the worship of Allah's Oneness, to abandon rivals to Him and to give up worshipping them. ﴿Then say, "Indeed, I am free of what you do"﴾ means: free of worshipping other than Allah, the Exalted, and not pleased with that from you nor in agreement with it, because it is forbidden and false shirk, which is blameworthy.

His saying ﴿And rely upon the Mighty﴾ means: the Overpowering, the Dominant, whom nothing that He wills can prevent, the Merciful toward His believing servants. The command to rely upon Him here is necessary, because He has commanded him to disavow the polytheists' shirk, and this position requires enmity toward them, plotting against them, and even fighting them. Hence it becomes obligatory to rely upon Allah and depend on Him; otherwise he would have no power to fight a people while being a single individual.

His saying ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: in your prayer, alone. ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾ means: and He sees your movement, standing, bowing and prostrating, along with the believing worshippers.

That is to say: He is with you, hearing and seeing, so rely upon Him, fear no one else, and press on with your call and your separation from the polytheists. His saying ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ confirms that special companionship, for the One who hears every sound and knows every movement and stillness is worthy of His servant's reliance and of entrusting the matter to Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of monotheism, and the prohibition of invoking other than Allah, exalted is He, among all His creatures, since that is forbidden shirk.

2- Whoever dies invoking other than Allah is certainly punished among the punished.

3- Affirmation of the principle of beginning with relatives in all matters, since they are closer to their kin than others are.

4- The legitimacy of gentleness and humility toward believers, especially those newly come to Islam.

5- The obligation to disavow shirk and its adherents.

6- The obligation to rely upon Allah and to carry out what Allah has made obligatory.

7- The virtue of night prayer and congregational prayer, because of the nearness of Allah's companionship that the servant attains.

﴿So do not invoke another god along with Allah, lest you be among those punished﴾: that is, do not worship another god alongside Allah, because du'a (supplication, invocation) is worship.

﴿And warn your closest kin﴾: they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib.

﴿And lower your wing﴾: that is, be gentle toward them.

﴿But if they disobey you﴾: that is, they refuse to accept your call to monotheism (tawhid) and reject what you call them to.

﴿Then say, "Indeed, I am free of what you do"﴾: that is, free of worshipping other than Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾: that is, to prayer, so you pray at night (tahajjud) alone.

﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾: that is, He sees your movements among the worshippers as you bow, prostrate and stand.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in seeking the guidance of Quraysh, the people of Muhammad ﷺ. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So do not invoke another god along with Allah, lest you be among those punished﴾, contains a clear allusion and indication that it is a rebuke to the polytheists who invoke idols as gods. It is a call that wakes them from their slumber: if the Messenger of Allah is forbidden to worship other than Allah, and would be punished among the punished if he did, then others are all the more so. The speech thus runs in the manner of "It is you I mean, but listen, O neighbour!" 

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And warn your closest kin﴾, is a command from Allah to His Messenger to first single out his relatives with his warning, since they are most entitled to seek their salvation from punishment. The Messenger carried out his Lord's command. It is reported in the Sahihs from Abu Hurayah (may Allah be pleased with him) that when the verse ﴿And warn your closest kin﴾ was revealed to him, he (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of Quraysh, purchase yourselves from Allah (meaning by faith and righteous deeds after abandoning polytheism and sins), for I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah, that is, against His punishment. O 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, ask me from my wealth whatever you wish; I cannot avail you anything against Allah."

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers﴾, is a command for him to be gentle toward the believers, to show them compassion and kindness, and to be pleasant to them, so that faith may take firm root in their hearts and they may be safe from the peril of apostasy, which might befall them if they were treated harshly and severely while they were at the beginning of the path to Allah, exalted is He.

His saying ﴿But if they disobey you﴾ means: those whom you have been commanded to call to the worship of Allah's Oneness, to abandon rivals to Him and to give up worshipping them. ﴿Then say, "Indeed, I am free of what you do"﴾ means: free of worshipping other than Allah, the Exalted, and not pleased with that from you nor in agreement with it, because it is forbidden and false shirk, which is blameworthy.

His saying ﴿And rely upon the Mighty﴾ means: the Overpowering, the Dominant, whom nothing that He wills can prevent, the Merciful toward His believing servants. The command to rely upon Him here is necessary, because He has commanded him to disavow the polytheists' shirk, and this position requires enmity toward them, plotting against them, and even fighting them. Hence it becomes obligatory to rely upon Allah and depend on Him; otherwise he would have no power to fight a people while being a single individual.

His saying ﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ means: in your prayer, alone. ﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾ means: and He sees your movement, standing, bowing and prostrating, along with the believing worshippers.

That is to say: He is with you, hearing and seeing, so rely upon Him, fear no one else, and press on with your call and your separation from the polytheists. His saying ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ confirms that special companionship, for the One who hears every sound and knows every movement and stillness is worthy of His servant's reliance and of entrusting the matter to Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of monotheism, and the prohibition of invoking other than Allah, exalted is He, among all His creatures, since that is forbidden shirk.

2- Whoever dies invoking other than Allah is certainly punished among the punished.

3- Affirmation of the principle of beginning with relatives in all matters, since they are closer to their kin than others are.

4- The legitimacy of gentleness and humility toward believers, especially those newly come to Islam.

5- The obligation to disavow shirk and its adherents.

6- The obligation to rely upon Allah and to carry out what Allah has made obligatory.

7- The virtue of night prayer and congregational prayer, because of the nearness of Allah's companionship that the servant attains.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 26, verses 221–227:

Explanation of the words:

Unabbi'ukum (I inform you): i.e., I tell you.

Affākin atheem (a great liar, sinful): i.e., a liar who turns lies around until they become falsehood, a person steeped in sins.

Yulqoon al-sam' (they lend their ears): i.e., they lend their ears and listen with the utmost attention to the devils, so they receive from them, most of which is lies and falsehood.

Al-ghāwūn (the errant): plural of ghāwin: one who has strayed from guidance, corrupt of heart and intention.

Fī kulli wād (in every valley): i.e., among the valleys of speech and its various kinds.

Yahīmūn (they wander): i.e., they proceed in every path and valley of speech, in praise or blame, whether it is true or false.

Yaqūlūna mā lā yaf'alūn (they say what they do not do): i.e., they say "we did" when they did not do.

Wantasarū min ba'di mā zulimū (and they defend themselves after they have been wronged): i.e., they composed poetry in defense of the truth by answering those who satirized the Muslims.

Ayya munqalabin yanqalibūn (what a return they will return to): i.e., the place to which they will return after death, which is the hellfire.

Meaning of the verses:

When the wrongdoers among the polytheists of Quraysh claimed that the Messenger ﷺ receives [revelation] from the devils the way soothsayers receive from them, Allah the Exalted refuted them, saying: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ And He answered the question, saying: ﴿They descend upon every lying sinner﴾: a liar who turns lies around, so that he calls the wrongdoer just, the wicked good, and the corrupt righteous. ﴿Sinner﴾: i.e., one who commits many sins, for he leaves no crime uncommitted and no evil undone, until he drowns in sin. This is the one with whom the devils unite and to whom they convey what they hear from the heaven, because he is like them in the darkness of the soul and the wickedness of the spirit. As for Muhammad ﷺ, he is the furthest of people from lying and sin; no lie was ever attributed to him, and no sin was ever known of him, ever. So how could the devils unite with him, inform him, and convey to him news of the heaven? By this the accusation is nullified. And His saying ﴿They lend their ears, and most of them are liars﴾: i.e., before the devils were prevented from eavesdropping by the placing of shooting stars to guard against them, they used to lend their ears to obtain news, and most of them were liars, for they would mix with the one word they heard a hundred words, all of which were lies, and they would convey that falsehood to their brethren in disbelief and wickedness among the soothsayers of mankind.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And the poets—the errant follow them﴾: i.e., the people of error and misguidance are those who follow the poets, relating from them and transmitting their words, and believing them in what they say. The proof of this is ﴿that they﴾, i.e., the poets, ﴿in every valley﴾ of the valleys of speech and its kinds, ﴿wander﴾ in their own direction, persisting in their saying, praising and blaming, satirizing, boasting, and claiming that they did such and such when they did not. So is Muhammad ﷺ, whom you accused of being a poet, and what he says is of the kind of poetry, are his followers errant? Look at them, ask about them, for they are the most rightly guided of people, the most righteous in deed, the most truthful in speech, and the furthest from doubt. As for Muhammad ﷺ, he is the furthest of people from lying and sin; no lie was ever attributed to him, and no sin was ever known of him, ever. So how could the devils unite with him, inform him, and convey to him news of the heaven? By this the accusation is nullified. And His saying ﴿They lend their ears, and most of them are liars﴾: i.e., before the devils were prevented from eavesdropping by the placing of shooting stars to guard against them, they used to lend their ears to obtain news, and most of them were liars, for they would mix with the one word they heard a hundred words, all of which were lies, and they would convey that falsehood to their brethren in disbelief and wickedness among the soothsayers of mankind.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And the poets—the errant follow them﴾: i.e., the people of error and misguidance are those who follow the poets, relating from them and transmitting their words, and believing them in what they say. The proof of this is ﴿that they﴾, i.e., the poets, ﴿in every valley﴾ of the valleys of speech and its kinds, ﴿wander﴾ in their own direction, persisting in their saying, praising and blaming, satirizing, boasting, and claiming that they did such and such when they did not. So is Muhammad ﷺ, whom you accused of being a poet, and what he says is of the kind of poetry, are his followers errant? Look at them, ask about them, for they are the most rightly guided of people, the most righteous in deed, the most truthful in speech, and the furthest from doubt. Had Muhammad been a poet, his followers would have been errant. Thus the claim is nullified from its foundation.

And His saying ﴿except those who believe, do righteous deeds, remember Allah much, and defend themselves after they have been wronged﴾: when He condemned the poets, He excepted from them such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha and Hassan ibn Thabit, who believed, did righteous deeds, and defended themselves, answering the satire of the polytheists against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and defending Islam and its people with their sincere, pure, clean, and faithful poetry.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And those who wronged will know what a return they will return﴾: i.e., those who wronged the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by accusing him of soothsaying at one time and of poetry at another, and who wronged the divine revelation by describing it with what is far from it, of soothsaying and poetry. ﴿What a return they will return﴾: i.e., what return they will return to; it is the Fire, and wretched is the abode.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Refutation of the polytheists' slander that the Qur'an is of the same kind as what soothsayers say.

2- Refutation that the Messenger ﷺ is a soothsayer or a poet.

3- Explanation that devils unite with those of wicked spirits in falsehood and sins.

4- Explanation that the followers of the falsifying poets, in every time and place, are the errant and misguided.

5- Permissibility of composing poetry and speaking it to establish knowledge or record wisdom, or to defend Islam and Muslims by answering those who satirize Islam and Muslims.

6- Warning against the consequences of wrongdoing, for they are grave.
